# Condor of Provider Pay (`condor-of-provider-pay`)

Works out provider pay by work RVU: wRVUs per provider from charges and your RVU file (with modifier adjustments), pay under tiered rates, and the true-up against draws paid, plus codes with no RVU and charges with no rendering provider. Patient names on charges are masked before results reach the model.

**Condor never runs payroll or pays providers. Condor never changes a compensation plan.**

Kestrel ver 1 · Money recovery and practice finance · MIT · Node 20 or newer · local files only · patient and staff identifiers masked before results reach the model · built on [`kestrel-core`](../kestrel-core)

```bash
npx -y condor-of-provider-pay demo
npx -y condor-of-provider-pay mcp --root ./practice-files
```

## What the sample data shows

Fictional data only: a made-up practice, providers and patients. The work RVUs are rounded example values, not the current CMS file, and the comp plan is an example.

- [`charges-2026-q3.csv`](fixtures/charges-2026-q3.csv), [`rvus.csv`](fixtures/rvus.csv) and [`comp-plan.json`](fixtures/comp-plan.json) for July to September 2026 (one October charge is outside the period). Planted:
  - Rhea Lin: 1,160 wRVUs earn 53,320 under the default tiers against 50,000 in draws, so 3,320 is owed at true-up. Ten 99417 lines have no work RVU in the file.
  - Sam Otto: 674 wRVUs (20 bilateral injections with modifier 50 at 150%) earn 30,330 against 33,000 in draws, so 2,670 was paid ahead.
  - June Park: 710 wRVUs earn 29,060 under her own tiers against 27,000 in draws, so 2,060 is owed.
  - Five charge lines have no rendering provider.
- [`settings-typo.json`](fixtures/settings-typo.json) misspells a setting and is refused.

## Tools

| Tool | What it does | Policy |
|---|---|---|
| `condor_check` | List charges with no provider, codes with no RVU, and each provider's true-up against draws. | runs |
| `condor_write_report` | Write condor-provider-pay.csv (one row per item, with blank owner and decision columns) and condor-provider-pay.html into out_dir (default kestrel-out/condor). | runs |
| `condor_recall` | Search this agent's own memory of the customer's setup: accepted facts (in use) and facts waiting for a person. | runs |
| `condor_learn` | Propose one fact about the customer's setup for this agent to remember. | runs |
| `condor_accept_learning` | A named person accepts or rejects a fact waiting in this agent's memory. | one named click, even in Auto (`accept_learning`) |
| `condor_retire_memory` | A named person stops an accepted fact from applying. | one named click, even in Auto (`accept_learning`) |
| `payroll_submit` | Condor never runs payroll or pays providers. | refused |
| `comp_plan_change` | Condor never changes a compensation plan. | refused |

Any tool name not in this table is blocked, including names a model invents. Refused tools are listed so a model can see they exist and are refused.

### `condor_check` arguments

| Argument | What it is |
|---|---|
| `charges` (required) | Charge lines under --root: rendering provider, date of service, code, modifiers, units |
| `rvus` (required) | Your RVU file: code, modifier (optional), work RVU (from the CMS file year your plan uses) |
| `settings` (required) | Settings JSON with the comp plan: tiers, providers (tiers, draws), modifier_pct |
| `from` | First date of service in the period (YYYY-MM-DD) |
| `to` | Last date of service in the period (YYYY-MM-DD) |
| `status` | Only items with this status |
| `limit` | Most items to return to the model (the report file always has all of them) |

## Columns it reads

Tables can be CSV, TSV, semicolon- or pipe-separated text, Excel `.xlsx`, JSON or JSONL. Columns are matched by the names below (any case and punctuation), and by their usual names in German, French, Spanish, Portuguese, Italian, Japanese, Chinese and Korean. Dates become `YYYY-MM-DD`. Columns marked *masked* hold patient or staff identifiers.

The PointClickCare, MatrixCare and American HealthTech style names were written from public help pages and general knowledge, **not checked against real exports**. Run `npx condor-of-provider-pay inspect <file>` (column names and shapes only, never values) and name any column it misses in `remedy-sources.json`.

### Charges (`charges`)

| Column | Type | Read from |
|---|---|---|
| `provider` | text | Provider, Rendering Provider, Rendering, Clinician, Therapist, Physician, Doctor, Practitioner |
| `dos` | date | Date of Service, DOS, Service Date, Visit Date, Date, From DOS, Session Date, Appointment Date |
| `cpt` (required) | text | CPT, Code, Procedure, Procedure Code, CPT/HCPCS, HCPCS, Service Code, Proc Code |
| `modifiers` | text | Modifiers, Modifier, Mod, Mods, Modifier 1, Mod 1 |
| `units` | number | Units, Unit, Qty, Quantity, Days/Units, Service Units |
| `patient_id` | text (masked) | Patient ID, Patient #, Patient Number, MRN, Medical Record Number, Chart #, Chart Number, Account # |
| `patient_name` | text (masked) | Patient, Patient Name, Name, Client, Client Name, Member, Member Name, Beneficiary |

### RVU file (`rvus`)

| Column | Type | Read from |
|---|---|---|
| `code` (required) | text | Code, HCPCS, CPT, CPT/HCPCS |
| `modifier` | text | Modifier, Mod |
| `work_rvu` (required) | number | Work RVU, wRVU, Work, RVU |

## Settings file (`condor_settings`)

A small JSON file you pass by path. A misspelled setting is refused by name rather than ignored, so a typo never silently changes a check.

| Setting | What it does |
|---|---|
| `tiers` | Default pay per wRVU by marginal tier: [{ "up_to": 1000, "rate": 45 }, { "rate": 52 }] |
| `providers` | Per-provider tiers and draws paid, by provider name |
| `modifier_pct` | Percent of the work RVU credited with a modifier, when the RVU file has no row for it; replaces the default (50: 150, 51: 50, 62: 62.5, 80/82/AS: 16) |

## Memory

`condor_learn` only proposes a fact; nothing changes until a named person accepts it with `condor_accept_learning`, which is one click even in Auto. Facts live in a hash-chained file under `.remedy/memory/`; if the chain does not verify, no fact is used. Credentials, personal identifiers and text that reads like instructions to an AI are refused.

| Kind | What an accepted fact does |
|---|---|

## Install

Node 20 or newer. No other runtime dependencies besides `kestrel-core` and `remedy-core`.

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "condor-of-provider-pay": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": [
        "-y",
        "condor-of-provider-pay",
        "mcp",
        "--root",
        "/path/to/practice-files"
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

Claude Code: `claude mcp add condor-of-provider-pay -- npx -y condor-of-provider-pay mcp --root .`, or use the plugin files in this folder.

## CLI

```bash
condor-of-provider-pay tools                 # every tool, its policy and arguments
condor-of-provider-pay sources               # the columns each input is read from
condor-of-provider-pay inspect <file>        # how a file would be read (names and shapes, never values)
condor-of-provider-pay call condor_check '{"charges":"<charges>","rvus":"<rvus>","settings":"<settings>"}'
condor-of-provider-pay eval                  # the private eval cases on the fictional fixtures
condor-of-provider-pay demo
```

## Patient and staff data

Results go to an AI model, so identifiers are masked before they leave the agent: patient and staff names become stable pseudonyms such as `PT-3f9a1c2e`, record and account numbers become `MRN-…` or `ACCT-…`, and e-mails and phone numbers are removed, also inside free text. Report files written to disk keep real names because staff work from them: keep them in a folder only your staff can open. The shared tests check that no fictional identifier from the fixtures reaches any eval result, and the hostile-input check plants spreadsheet formulas, HTML and AI-aimed instructions in the data. This keeps PHI away from the model; it is **not** a HIPAA compliance determination. Your business associate agreements, access controls and policies still apply.

## Limits

- Reads only the files you give it. It does not log in to an EHR, practice-management system, payer portal, clearinghouse, state system, HR or payroll system, or bank.
- Payer, Medicare, Medicaid, state and federal rules are summarised from public material as of 2026, and the numbers are settings you supply; a billing, compliance or legal professional checks them before you rely on them.
- Not legal, billing, coding, tax, clinical or HIPAA advice. It does not diagnose or recommend care. A person decides what to bill, pay, report, file or send.
- Every call is written to a hash-chained audit log under `.remedy/` in the root. No network calls, no telemetry, no credentials. The bundled data is fictional.
